entry.title: PEEK: integrated primer design for silent-mutation and restriction-site engineering, validated in silico and by whole-plasmid sequencing
entry.summary:
Motivation: Silent introduction of restriction sites, direct site insertion, and verification of the result are routine operations in molecular cloning, yet they are typically distributed across separate tools built on inconsistent thermodynamics. Primer design is itself mature and heavily validated; the gap is not accuracy in principle but integration, together with the absence of any explicit account of why one synonymous edit should be preferred over another. Because melting temperature (Tm) gates which primers a tool will accept, any unified tool must first be shown to compute Tm correctly against an external standard, and then shown to produce the edits it proposes.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #distributed-systems #number-theory

entry.title: Pufferfish: DAG-Guided Speculative Execution for Low-Latency BFT SMR
entry.summary:
Modern Byzantine fault-tolerant state machine replication (BFT SMR) systems increasingly decouple data dissemination from transaction ordering, but typically execute transactions only after consensus finalizes their order. This execution-after-consensus design serializes ordering and execution on the confirmation path, so transactions incur both costs even under normal network conditions. Decoupling enables dissemination to continue during ordering stalls, but amplifies the same bottleneck: disseminated transactions accumulate into an execution backlog that replicas must drain after ordering recovers.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems #consensus

entry.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals -- by Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing
entry.summary:
We study California's short-term lodging price transparency law (AB 537), which from July 1, 2024 required Airbnb and other providers to advertise fee-inclusive prices. Using Coarsened Exact Matching to compare Airbnb listings in San Diego and San Francisco with those in Seattle and Chicago, we find that all-in pricing made guests more price-sensitive relative to control cities; yet, contrary to the standard prediction that transparency lowers prices, average daily rates rose by 4.8 percent. We also observe significant market churn: relative to control cities, treated cities saw more exits and entries, listings reliant on cleaning-fee revenue disproportionately exited, higher-quality listings were more likely to stay, and entrants offered lower fees and lower quality than incumbents.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #distributed-systems
